subject: Re: Urgent: Hosted API tail latency & 500s — possible KV/prefix cache misses
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@cardinalpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High tail latency & errors on /v1/generate (since 03/14 08:50)

Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency on your hosted API around 08:50 PT this morning. Our metrics show p95 jumping from ~220ms to ~2.1s and p99 hitting 5–6s intermittently. We're also seeing ~1.8% 500-level errors for requests routed to /v1/generate which is breaking our card authorization flow (timeouts causing payment retries).

We've throttled some traffic but the impact is customer-facing. Attached is a short span of our client-side traces and aggregated latencies. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (rollout, config, cache settings) that might cause prefix/KV cache misses or invalidation?

This is on the CardinalPay production account (company id 67890). We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can route us to a lower-latency fallback while you investigate.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform, CardinalPay
ops@cardinalpay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T09:19:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: High tail latency & errors on /v1/generate — CardinalPay production impact (URGENT)

Team — forwarding an escalated customer report (CardinalPay). Key points: p95 up to ~2.1s, p99 spikes 5–6s, ~1.8% 500s, started ~08:50 PT. Customer suspects cache invalidation/prefix misses.

Immediate asks:
- Can SRE/infra confirm whether we had a config push, cache-pruner change, or TTL modification impacting KV/prefix cache around 08:30–09:00 PT?
- If cache misses are elevated, what is the fastest mitigation (rollback, pin model, route traffic to dedicated pool, warm cache)?
- I'll coordinate communications and offer a temporary credit if needed; please mark any exec-sensitive items for Vivek.

Customer trace attached; linking incident once we open it.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency & errors on /v1/generate — CardinalPay production impact (URGENT)

Marissa / team — I see the same symptom in our telemetry. Cache miss ratio for the shared KV/prefix cache jumped at ~08:49 and there are correlated increases in GPU scheduling latency. I've attached a 30s trace and perf logs (perf-logs-20260314.zip).

Immediate notes:
- We deployed a change to cache-pruner config at 08:40 PT (small regex tweak intended to prune old prefixes) — rolling back now to last known good.
- Misses appear to be concentrated on a small set of hot prefixes used by high-concurrency payment flows (fits CardinalPay usage).
- Short-term mitigation: rollback pruner + run cache rewarm script (warmup should restore p95 in ~20–40m; p99 depends on backend re-replication).

I'll continue to run the rollback and monitor. Assigning Markus to help with rewarm and any routing toggles.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T09:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency & errors on /v1/generate — CardinalPay production impact (URGENT)

Confirmed — the cache-pruner change introduced a fuzzy regex that over-matched and invalidated many prefix keys. Rollback complete at 09:37 PT.

Action plan (now):
1) Run rewarm job for hot prefixes (runbook: runbook-cache-warmup.md). ETA p95 improvement: 20–35 minutes after warmup start. Expect p99 to improve gradually over the following hour as cached KV entries re-propagate.
2) If degradation persists, we can failover CardinalPay's traffic to the Dedicated pool for 30–60 minutes (requires approval from Product ops but is a straightforward routing rule).
3) Opened INF-10234 and attached diff for the change: cache-pruner-config.diff

I've started the warmup now (09:41 PT). Attaching SLO dashboard screenshot: slo-dashboard-20260314.png

—Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: High tail latency & errors on /v1/generate (since 03/14 08:50)

Alex — quick update and immediate action we're taking: 

What happened (interim): our infra team rolled back a cache-pruner config change that inadvertently invalidated hot prefix/KV entries. That rollback completed at 09:37 PT and we've started a cache rewarm job for the hot prefixes that CardinalPay uses.

Short-term mitigation provided:
- Rollback completed; rewarm in progress (expected p95 recovery in 20–35 minutes, p99 improving over 1+ hour).
- If you prefer, we can failover a percentage of your traffic to a dedicated pool while warmup completes — let me know a target percentage and I will coordinate.
- We're opening an incident page and will share a full postmortem within 72 hours.

We're very sorry for the disruption. If you'd like an exec call while we stabilize, I'm happy to set it up immediately.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

1) We need an incident page we can share internally (status link).
2) Please confirm whether this was a one-off human config push or if the config is generated by CI (we need to understand risk of recurrence).

Appreciate the fast rollback. We'll monitor and let you know if anything changes.

—Alex
